text:
maya: quick sync — thinking through how the smokehouse should plug into the admission pipeline. want to align on gating contracts and what counts as a hard vs soft failure.

devin: +1. do you mean the lightweight smoke that runs on ingest + the staged replay? or a single unified smoke harness?

maya: unified-ish. goal: cheap, fast checks that catch obvious runtime incompat and perf regressions before benching. timeline-wise it runs immediately on intake and again in pre-canary.

alessio: examples of "obvious"? model failing to load, OOM in KV restore, runtime mismatch (e.g. aten ops), or insane latency tail. also quantized model shape mismatches.

kat: also tokenization mismatches — we had a regression where tokenizer truncated differently and app-level prompts blew up. smoke should run a few canonical prompts.

devin: propose two tiers: "smoke-fast" (30s): load, single infer on 3 prompts, KV warmup, simple perf numbers (p50/p95). fails are hard. "smoke-deep" (5-10m): more sequences, vary len, check cache correctness, and run a small eval set for quality deltas — soft failures that flag but don't block if fallback exists.

maya: that matches my thinking. need to codify exact metrics and thresholds. for perf: p95 latency > 2x baseline => hard fail? or soft?

alessio: 2x p95 seems severe as hard fail for new model families. maybe: >3x p50 or >2.5x p95 => soft-fail with auto-fallback to lower-cost variant. hard fail for startup OOM, model load error, or mismatch in exported ops.

kat: for quality drift: klinch at >5% regression in key eval metrics should block for human review. but we should be conservative with automatic hard blocks — want to avoid blocking useful models for slight eval noise.

devin: agreed. we can make the thresholds configurable per-tenant and per-model-family. defaults: smoke-fast hard failures = load error, runtime exception, KV corruption. smoke-deep soft failures = perf regression thresholds, tokenizer diffs, minor output delta.

maya: how to represent these in the admission API? we need a compact handshake so the intake service can decide return code and set rollout policy hints. thoughts on payload?

alessio: simple JSON contract from smoke runner: {status: "pass|soft_fail|hard_fail", checks: [{name, result, details, metric, threshold}], artifact_refs: [onnx/ggml/etc], runner_version}. keep it flat and stable.

devin: +1. also include model fingerprints: schema, param-count, dtype (fp16/int8), max_seq, kv-cache-expected-keys. this helps quick compatibility logic in the router.

kat: we should add a checksum of tokenizer vocab and a quick hash of model signature to detect accidental re-exports.

maya: for smoke runner implementation, can we reuse current bench harness components? avoid duplicating heavy infra.

devin: yes — take lightweight pieces from bench: loader, sample prompts, tokenization comparator, and a minimal perf probe. keep dependencies minimal so smoke runs on lower-tier machines.

alessio: critical: make smoke idempotent and timeboxed. if it exceeds X seconds mark as soft-fail and attach partial results. otherwise we get stuck ingestion pipelines.

maya: agree. make hard timeout 60s for smoke-fast, 600s for smoke-deep. partial results on timeout.

sre-bot: test-run 2405123550: smoke-fast on model redwood/sample-1 completed: status=soft_fail; p95=1.9x baseline; tokenizer/hash mismatch=true. artifacts uploaded to s3://smoke-results/2405123550.json

devin: saw the bot output. tokenizer mismatch urgent — could be tokenizers v0.18 vs v0.19 mismatch. alessio, can the loader detect tokenizer lib differences and attempt deterministic tokenization with our bundled tokenizer as fallback?

alessio: we can. fallback path: if tokenizer hash differs, run our bundled tokenization and include both token sequences in details. that'll help reviewers see the delta.

kat: user-visible behaviour: if tokenizer mismatch only, we should soft-fail but still allow canary if human ok. otherwise reject. add an alert to the intake runbook for tokenizer mismatches.

maya: ops: add a flag to intake to mark "allow_soft_fail": boolean. default false for enterprise tenants, true for internal/staging. this controls whether soft failures block ingestion.

devin: rollout implications — for models that soft-fail for perf, route them to dedicated capacity or slower TIER until manual signoff. we already have routing policies; just add a new tag from admission: candidate_tier: [dedicated, burst, hosted-slow].

alessio: implementation note: the smoke runner should produce a single-line status that the intake can parse without heavy parsing. also attach a full JSON for bookkeeping.

kat: what about quantized casts? smoke should verify that int8 path produces stable logits within epsilon. we should include a small set of logits comparison checks and a diff threshold.

devin: agree. add 'logit_l2' and 'topk-stability' checks. those are cheap with a handful of prompts.

maya: action items: 1) devin: draft the JSON contract and default thresholds (due EOD Fri). 2) alessio: prototype tokenizer-fallback and timeout handling (PR next week). 3) kat: update intake runbook with soft-fail workflow and tenant flag (first draft Mon). 4) maya: write short RFC follow-up doc linking these decisions + example outputs.

archie: pinging infra — we'll need a smoke runner queue with cheap workers. can we reuse the preflight pool?

devin: yes reuse preflight, but isolate via low-priority queue and limited concurrency. add a circuit-breaker if queue backlog > N.

maya: sounds good. last Q: telemetry — add counters for smoke pass/soft/hard and average durations. also link smoke result id to model entry in registry for debugging.

alessio: noted. we'll add smoke_result_id in registry record.

maya: cool. if no objections I'll turn this into a short RFC note and draft the contract. thanks everyone. :slightly_smiling_face:
